description: Per-component UI copy writing rules. Shared prefix vocabulary is factored out once; each component references which prefixes apply.

shared_prefix_format.description: Prefix precedes the title, separated by a space. Applies to Alert Dialog, Inline Alert, and Alert Banner titles when the component calls for a specific user action.

prefixes.meaning: user must complete a step to proceed / do something to restore full functionality / fix something in this section
a workflow gate; someone must sign off before continuing
no hard block, but the user should look at this before moving on / before continuing
time-sensitive or security-related; reserved for genuine urgency, not a substitute for Action Required; use sparingly

shared_prefix_format.skip_when: Purely informational or destructive confirmation dialogs where no remediation action exists; system outages or read-only informational content; neutral or informational variants.

components.name: Alert Dialog
components.when_to_use: The user must acknowledge or decide before continuing. High consequence. Blocking.
components.golden_rule: The user is already interrupted. Be efficient.

structure.limit: 30–60 characters, no end punctuation, max 2 lines

title_rules: Communicate the result or the required decision, not the cause
description_rules: Include error codes in parentheses at the end of the last sentence
action_button_rules: Secondary = exit or undo (Cancel, Discard changes, Skip for now, Remind me later)

variants.name: Confirmation
variants.description: user confirms a choice; primary highlights preferred action

variants.name: Informative
variants.description: notable info to acknowledge; use toast instead if no action needed

variants.name: Destructive
variants.description: permanent, negative impact on data; primary button is red

variants.name: Warning
variants.description: user should be aware but isn't blocked; yellow warning icon

variants.name: Error
variants.description: user may be blocked; consider inline alert if no specific action is required

components.name: Toast
components.when_to_use: Confirming a completed action. Low priority. No required response. Auto-dismisses.
rules: Sentence case, no period, max 90 characters, max 2 lines
Must be instantly understandable: if it needs explanation, don't use a toast
Don't use for promotional messages, upsells, or proactive/preventative information
Max 1 action (undo, fix, show, update)

variants.name: Success/Confirmation
variants.sentence_construction: short past participle phrase: "(noun) + verb-ed + (optional detail)"

variants.name: Neutral (gray)
variants.sentence_construction: no icon; use when semantic variants don't fit

components.name: Inline Alert
components.when_to_use: Contextual to a section of the page. The user can continue without acting. Consequence is real but not blocking.

structure.limit: optional, for additional detail in a new tab

rules: Describe what happened, why, and what they can do
Don't repeat or restate the title in the description

example.title: Premium may change
example.body: Adjusting the effective date can increase or decrease your total premium.

variants.name: Neutral (gray)
variants.example: Payment information / Enter your billing address…

variants.name: Informative (blue)
variants.example: Accepted payment methods / Only major credit cards are accepted…

variants.name: Positive (green)
variants.example: Purchase completed / You'll get a confirmation email shortly.

variants.name: Notice (yellow)
variants.example: Update payment information / The saved credit card has expired.

components.name: Helper Text
components.when_to_use: Attached directly to a form field. Instructs correct input or surfaces a field-level error.
rules: Under 50 characters, 1 line or 1 short sentence
Neutral state: describes the solution proactively, before the user makes an error
Error state: describes the solution, not the error: tell them how to fix it, not what they did wrong
Error state uses a red warning icon

examples.neutral: Password must be at least 8 characters.
examples.negative: Create a password with at least 8 characters. (triggered after bad input)

components.name: Alert Banner
components.when_to_use: System-level message. Affects the whole app or a major capability. High visibility, persistent until resolved.
rules: Never auto-dismisses: persists until resolved (reappears on refresh if dismissed without fixing)
Max 1 action per banner
Max 2 lines in smaller viewports

structure.limit: 20–40 characters; emphasized lead-in text, flows naturally into the description
50–140 characters, no period on short phrases; impact + consequence + connects to the action

action_types: Secondary button: takes user to fix the issue
Link button: takes user to learn more

variants.name: Neutral (gray)
variants.description: concise message with optional recommended action

variants.name: Informative (blue)
variants.description: system-level context, include action when possible

variants.name: Error (red)
variants.description: system-level failure, include action when possible

components.name: Tooltip
components.when_to_use: Adding a label or short description to an interactive element on hover or keyboard focus.
rules: 40–60 characters max, 2 lines max
Only on interactive elements
Never duplicates the visible label of the trigger element
No actions inside tooltips
Don't use to add "nice to have" context: only essential labels or descriptions

components.name: Empty State
components.when_to_use: A list, page, or section has nothing to show. Not an error. Covers first use, a user-cleared list, and no search results.

structure.limit: 15–40 characters, no end punctuation; says what's missing or what this place is for
40–120 characters, 1–2 sentences; doesn't restate the title

rules: Say why it's empty only when that helps the user act
Give a next step that fills the space. The exception is no results, where the next step is changing the search or filter
Never blame the user
No filler. Every word either explains or points to the next step
Don't restate the title in the description
Personality follows `rhetorical-devices`: one device at most, first use only. Never on user-cleared or no-results states

variants.name: First use
variants.description: the user hasn't created anything yet; explain what fills this space and how to start
variants.example: No invoices yet / Create an invoice and it shows up here. / Create invoice

variants.name: User cleared
variants.description: the user finished or removed everything; confirm it, then offer the next item
variants.example: All tasks done / Add a task to plan your next steps. / Add task

variants.name: No results
variants.description: a search or filter matched nothing; the next step is changing the query, not creating content
variants.example: No results for "invoice 204" / Try a different search or clear your filters. / Clear filters

variants.name: Empty by nature
variants.description: zero rows is the normal, good state, such as no live calls or no open issues; say so plainly and add no action
variants.example: No open issues / Nothing needs your attention right now.

variants.name: No access
variants.description: the user's role cannot see any rows; say that access is the reason and who can grant it, and never offer a create action
variants.example: You don't have access to invoices / Ask an admin to add you to the Billing team.

components.name: Permission Prompt
components.when_to_use: The app is about to ask for a device or account permission: location, notifications, camera, contacts, or storage. Also applies to a priming screen shown before the native OS dialog.

structure.limit: 40–80 characters, one sentence; leads with what the user gets
optional, 60–150 characters; adds one concrete detail
verb plus the permission name, 2–3 words
exit with no penalty, 2 words, such as "Not now"

rules: Lead with the benefit to the user, then name the permission in the action
Ask in context, when the user first reaches the feature that needs it. Never on launch
The primary action names the permission and matches what the OS dialog asks for
State one specific benefit. Don't write "we need access"
If the user declines, the follow-up copy says what they'll miss and how to change it later. No guilt, no repeated asks
On a priming screen before the OS dialog, the same rules apply and the primary action opens the OS dialog

example.benefit_line: Get alerts when your order ships.

components.declined_example: You won't get shipping alerts. Turn them on anytime in Settings.

good: Get alerts when your order ships. / Allow notifications
See stores near you. / Allow location
bad: We need access to your notifications.

components.name: Prefill badge and source line
components.when_to_use: A field or answer holds a value the user did not type this session: from a profile, a link, an earlier answer, or an AI guess.
components.golden_rule: Say where the value came from, and make it easy to change.
rules: Badge: 2 to 5 words, sentence case, no period. Name the source in plain words
Source line: under 60 characters. Say 'Source:' then where it came from
Never show a confidence percentage. Use a word such as Likely, or show the source instead
After the user edits, the badge becomes 'Edited by you'
'Not me' clears every prefilled identity field in one tap
Undo message: say what was cleared, with one Undo action
When two sources disagree, show both values and let the user pick

variants.name: Sources disagree
variants.sentence_construction: Your profile says X. Last time you said Y.

components.name: Selection limit and count
components.when_to_use: A multiple choice question has a minimum, a maximum, or an exclusive option.
components.golden_rule: State the rule before the user answers. Explain every disabled option.
rules: Helper states the limit before the answer: 'Select up to 3'
Count updates live: '2 of 3 selected'
At the max, say why options are disabled and how to free one
Exclusive option: say it clears the others
Never say 'invalid selection'. Say what to do

variants.name: Max reached
variants.sentence_construction: Maximum reached. Deselect one to choose another.
examples: Maximum reached. Deselect one to choose another.

variants.name: Exclusive
variants.sentence_construction: Choosing X clears your other choices
examples: Choosing 'None of these' clears your other choices.

variants.name: Error
variants.sentence_construction: Select at least N. You selected M.

good: Maximum reached. Deselect one to choose another.

components.name: Availability check
components.when_to_use: The system checks whether a value is free or valid on the server, such as a name, handle, or code.
components.golden_rule: Say what is happening, what the result means, and what to do next.
rules: Checking: 2 to 3 words, shown only if the check takes more than a moment
Available: say so in 1 to 2 words. Do not celebrate
Taken: say it is taken and suggest the next step. Do not blame
Cannot check: say the check failed and that the user can continue
Never reveal whether an account exists for a sensitive value

variants.name: Cannot check
variants.sentence_construction: Couldn't check right now. We'll check again when you submit.
examples: Couldn't check right now. We'll check again when you submit.

bad: Oops! Someone beat you to it!

components.name: One-time code and resend
components.when_to_use: The user enters a one-time code and may ask for another.
components.golden_rule: Tell them where the code went and when they can ask again.
rules: Say where the code was sent without showing the full address or number
Show the wait as a plain countdown
Resend is a button once the wait ends
A wrong code says the code did not match and what to do. It does not say how close it was
An expired code says it expired and offers a new one

variants.name: Sent
variants.sentence_construction: We sent a code to + masked target

variants.name: Wrong code
variants.sentence_construction: That code didn't match. Check it and try again.
examples: That code didn't match. Check it and try again.

variants.name: Expired
variants.sentence_construction: That code expired. Send a new one.
examples: That code expired. Send a new one.

bad: Please wait before requesting another code

components.name: Saved state and drafts
components.when_to_use: A long form or questionnaire saves answers, restores a draft, or a link would replace a saved draft.
components.golden_rule: Never use a modal to say something was saved.
rules: Saved state is a quiet inline word, not a toast or modal
Failed save says it did not save and offers Retry
Save and finish later states how long the draft is kept
A link that would overwrite a saved draft asks before it does
Name both choices with verbs

variants.name: Finish later
variants.sentence_construction: We'll keep your answers for N days.
examples: We'll keep your answers for 30 days.

variants.name: Overwrite warning
variants.title: You have a saved draft
variants.sentence_construction: Continue the saved draft or start with the link's answers?

bad: Your progress has been successfully saved!

components.name: Questionnaire errors
components.when_to_use: The respondent presses Next and one or more questions fail a check.
components.golden_rule: Say what to fix on each question, in the place it needs fixing.
rules: Banner: count the problems, then link to each
Inline error: say what to do and what happened. Under 60 characters
Required is a plain word, not an asterisk alone
Never say 'invalid'. Never blame the respondent

variants.name: Too few
variants.sentence_construction: Select at least N. You selected M.

components.name: Progress and review
components.when_to_use: A questionnaire shows where the respondent is, a review screen, or a confirmation.
components.golden_rule: Honest counts, and say what happens after Submit.
rules: Progress text: 'Question n of N' or 'Section n of N'. Never a bare percentage
Review screen title says what to do: Review your answers
Confirmation says it worked, what was received, and what happens next
Skipped-by-logic answers show as removed on Review

variants.name: Confirmation
variants.sentence_construction: Title: what worked. Body: what we got and what happens next.
examples: We'll use them to plan the next release. You don't need to do anything else.

components.name: Rank prompts
components.when_to_use: The respondent ranks items by dragging, or with the up and down buttons.
components.golden_rule: Say how to rank, and say what changed after every move.
rules: Helper says how: press and hold, then drag, or use the arrows
Say the limit when it is the top N
Each move is announced in full: item, new position, total
Never make drag the only way

variants.name: Helper
variants.sentence_construction: Press and hold an item, then drag it into place. Your top N count.
examples: Press and hold an item, then drag it into place. Your top 3 count.

variants.name: Position
variants.sentence_construction: Item, moved to position n of N
examples: Battery life, moved to position 2 of 6

variants.name: Cutoff
variants.sentence_construction: Your top N end here. Items below are not ranked.
examples: Your top 3 end here. Items below are not ranked.

good: Press and hold an item, then drag it into place. Your top 3 count.

components.name: Poll and quiz results
components.when_to_use: After a respondent answers a choice question, the screen shows how others answered, and in a quiz which option is correct.
components.golden_rule: Say what the numbers are out of, and say the result in words, not only in color.
rules: Mark the right option with the words 'Correct answer'. Mark the respondent's pick with 'Your answer'
Give the count in plain words: '1 vote', '42 votes'. Never 'votes: 42'
Under the minimum, say there are too few votes. Do not show a percent or count
For multi-select, say the percents add up to more than 100%
The announcement is one short sentence about this respondent's result. It does not list every option
Do not cheer or console. 'Not quite' is enough for a wrong answer

variants.name: Too few votes
variants.sentence_construction: Too few votes to show results yet.
examples: Too few votes to show results yet.

variants.name: Multi-select note
variants.sentence_construction: Each percent is out of everyone who answered. They add up to more than 100%.
examples: Each percent is out of everyone who answered. They add up to more than 100%.

variants.name: Announcement, wrong answer
variants.sentence_construction: Not quite. The correct answer is X.
examples: Not quite. The correct answer is 366. 62% of people chose it.

variants.name: Announcement, poll
variants.sentence_construction: Results are in. N people answered.

good: Not quite. The correct answer is 366.
